It has become clear from the above discussion that overlap capacitances must be as small as
possible. On top of that, some more parasitic capacitances have to be added.
For example, in the layout on the left, the poly Gate lines cross the Source and Drain lines.
The crossing areas (black) give coupling capacitances to be added to the overlap capacitances.

commentary_segments.text: The clock feedthrough will now be increased. Such layout is thus better avoided. The best that can be achieved is to use as small a MOST switch as possible, as shown in the middle. The overlap capacitances are also as small as possible as they scale with the widths of the MOSTs. On the right, an example is given on the use of metal shields between the clock lines and the actual MOSTs, reducing the coupling capacitances.

The clock feedthrough will now be increased. Such layout is thus better avoided. The best that can be achieved is to use as small a MOST switch as possible, as shown in the middle. The overlap capacitances are also as small as possible as they scale with the widths of the MOSTs. On the right, an example is given on the use of metal shields between the clock lines and the actual MOSTs, reducing the coupling capacitances.
